name: Mortar Calculator
description: Calculate mortar volume, pre-mix mortar bags, Portland cement, and masonry sand for brick and concrete block walls.
search_intent: Calculate how much mortar is needed for laying bricks or concrete masonry blocks.
keywords: how many bags of mortar do i need

inputs.label: Number of masonry units (bricks or blocks)
Masonry unit type (standard brick vs 8-inch CMU block)
inputs.help: standard brick (approx 4.5 to 5.5 ft³ mortar per 1000 bricks) vs 8x8x16 CMU block (approx 13 to 15 ft³ mortar per 100 blocks)

calculation: Base yield: Standard modular bricks use approximately 5.0 ft³ of mortar per 1,000 units at 3/8-inch joint. Standard 8x8x16 CMU blocks use approximately 13.5 ft³ of mortar per 100 blocks at 3/8-inch bed and head joints. Scale volume proportionally by joint thickness ratio (thickness / 0.375). Total adjusted volume = base volume × (1 + waste / 100). Pre-mix bags: 80-lb bag yields approximately 0.67 ft³; 60-lb bag yields 0.50 ft³. Site-mix Type N ratio (1 part cement to 3 parts damp loose sand): 1 bag (94 lb) cement + 3 ft³ sand yields approx 3.2 ft³ mixed mortar. Whole bags round upward with ceil.
limitations: Mortar volume depends on brick coring, frog recesses, and CMU face-shell bedding vs full bedding.
Site-mixed mortar requires verified proportioning complying with ASTM C270 (Type N, S, or M).
Weather conditions and tooling loss can affect actual field yield.
